family.line: Anthony uses a wheelchair. His son Justin is immobile and has cerebral palsy.

night.line: The night the 2025 LA fires started, Anthony began calling for assistance to evacuate.

calls.line: In the following hours, he called 911 twice, but nobody came.

gone.line: Two hours later, he and his son both passed away in their home.

everywhere.line: From wildfires to hurricanes, there are thousands of cases like Anthony and Justin’s.

eighty.line: A UN survey found that 80% of people with disabilities would not be able to evacuate without difficulty during emergencies.

howSave.line: So how could we have saved Anthony and Justin?

stations.line: During Cal Hacks, we talked to firefighters, station chiefs, and battalion officers who told us that the problem was figuring out who needs help and how to most effectively use their limited equipment and personnel.

dispatch.line: Particularly, during emergencies, underfunded and understaffed dispatch teams are quickly overwhelmed by thousands of calls.

built.line: That’s why we built Standard Response.

tenThousand.line: AI agents can now hold 10,000 real conversations on the phone at the same time.

zone.line: Standard Response calls every household in the evacuation radius,

census.line: creating a network census with who needs help, who can help, and where people are.

roseland.line: Here's a test call we did with my grandma, Roseland.

ink.line: Cartesia’s Ink model listens to Roseland in 10 languages

sonic.line: and Sonic speaks the agent’s replies back to her.

claude.line: Claude’s Haiku and Opus models power the logic and alignment of the AI voice agent system,

protocol.line: which makes every reply aligned with real 911 protocols.

request.line: After Roseland’s request gets added to the rescue map,

alns.line: We use the data collected to run an ALNS optimization algorithm,

routes.line: efficiently routing neighbors and first responders towards people who most urgently need help, saving time and lives.

crowd.line: We simulate everyone leaving the area as particles under Langevin dynamics, modelling congestion

jams.line: so first responders can see the real ETAs rather than google maps estimates.

maria.line: Maria answers the phone and says she can help.

hub.line: Everything on our system shares one Convex database,

stress.line: whose reliability we stress-tested in handling mission critical concurrent reads and writes.

nights.line: We put the whole system through 100 simulated fire nights with households modeled on real data and 911 calls.

today.line: When riders had to reach 911 themselves, only 4% of the people who needed help got out in time.

quote.line: An EMT and Firefighter we spoke to said Standard Response “Is the most cutting-edge EMT improvement idea I’ve heard”

told.line: 911 told Anthony Mitchell “help is on their way,” but nobody came.

reached.line: Standard Response strives so that that will never happen again.

everyone.line: So for all of the Anthonys, Justins, and Roselands out there,

saveLives.line: let’s save lives, one call and one response at a time.
